name: Symbol Resolver
responsibility: Turns a free-text or ticker query into a bound instrument: fuzzy/exact matching over the NSE+BSE master lists, marquee-collision disambiguation, and the single acceptance-threshold policy (resolution_policy.py) every consumer must go through. Owns the offline master-list regeneration scripts (BSE master, India sector map, NSE symbol-change history).

name: Fundamentals & Profile Contract (field_meta)
responsibility: The company-profile data contract: per-field provenance/staleness (field_meta) on every fundamentals value, the warm-cache seed/store lifecycle, and the REST + agent-tool surface that serves it. types/data.ts is the hand-mirrored TS side of the same contract (CLAUDE.md gotcha: change both in one commit).

name: Disclosures & Witnesses (BSE XBRL, ownership)
responsibility: R13's data-trust layer: parses BSE XBRL shareholding disclosures, cross-checks promoter/institutional ownership, and runs the independent 'witnesses' (52-week range, market-cap, earnings-quality) that catch a plausible-but-wrong figure a single provider would let through.

name: Research Engine: Retrieval & Relevance
responsibility: The funnel's first two stages: a multi-backend keyless/keyed web-search abstraction (SearXNG, Brave, DDG, Mojeek) with a circuit breaker and pacing, then the relevance filter that decides which retrieved results survive into extraction. Named in the brief as the prime suspect for the operator's 'web search bugging out' complaint.

name: Research Engine: Extraction & Synthesis
responsibility: Turns surviving search results into a cited brief: page extraction, financial-semantics tagging, citation verification, and the brief data contract (types/brief.ts) plus its frontend claim-ingest/normalisation helpers that keep a re-published brief from losing its structured metrics.

name: Research Engine: Depth / Iteration / Deep
responsibility: The two-tier depth ladder (FAST vs full/deep) and its iteration loop: target binding, self-verification pass, and the hosted-deep-research routing (Tongyi/OpenRouter fallback) that the agent_tools research/deep_research entry points expose to the chat agent.

name: Agent Runtime
responsibility: The tool-calling loop itself: turn assembly, per-provider metadata quirks (Gemini function_response pairing, tool-call/tool-result turns), the first-party agent roster (JSON personas), and custom-agent CRUD. FLAG: correctness_gate.py and model_registry.py are load-bearing here but owned by market-data-providers / llm-adapters respectively.

name: Agent Tools + Capability Catalog + Ack Ledger
responsibility: catalog.py is the single source of truth every tool schema, allow-list and MCP projection derives from (Constitution Principle II). Bundles the cross-domain read-only agent tools not already owned by a domain subsystem, plus action_ledger.py, the ack/confirmation ledger backing the confirm-before-place safety gate. FLAG: action_ledger.py is also load-bearing for safety-audit.

name: Screener
responsibility: Full-stack cold/warm stock screener: the India universe + formula DSL/parser on the backend, the criteria-builder + pasted-formula UI on the frontend, and the agent tool that lets a chat turn author a screen. workflow_nodes/screener_nodes.py lives with workflow-engine (FLAG: shares screener.py's formula evaluator).

name: Backtest
responsibility: Full-stack strategy backtesting: the bar-replay engine, a small strategy DSL plus canned strategies, persisted run history, and the panel + custom-strategy code editor on the frontend. backtest_agent_parity test pins that the agent tool and UI path produce identical results.

name: Portfolio
responsibility: Paper-portfolio persistence and P&L: SQLite-backed positions/lots, the metrics module (unrealised P&L, weights), the panel, and the agent-facing broker_portfolio read tool that lets an agent see (never place into) a connected broker's holdings alongside paper ones.

name: Plugins (Contract + Bootstrap + Bundled)
responsibility: The VystedPlugin Tier-1 contract (types/plugin.ts, 6 capabilities), the PLUGIN_COMPANIONS static-import bridge that lets a serializable contract still ship React panels, and every bundled non-broker plugin. Broker plugins live in brokers-adapters (FLAG: both subsystems touch plugins/brokers/*/manifest.json's declared capabilities).

name: LLM Provider Adapters
responsibility: Per-provider chat/tool-call adapters (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Groq, Ollama, OpenRouter) behind one base interface, the model/pricing single-source-of-truth (model_registry.py + its JSON), and the frontend provider-key/model-picker stores. Owns the two OpenAI tool-time 400 traps documented in CLAUDE.md.

name: Error Layer
responsibility: The one place a raw provider/HTTP failure becomes a typed, user-legible frame: sidecar-side error normalisation (errors.py), the frontend's FastAPI-validation-error parsing in the shared API client, and the chat-stream error/notice frames (MessageErrorFrame, StreamErrorFrame) rendered in the composer. FLAG: message-notices.ts/streaming.ts are also core chat-UI files (frontend-panels-agent-shell).

name: Runs / Durable Delegate
responsibility: Detached long-running agent execution: run_manager spawns asyncio tasks driving invoke_agent with SQLite-backed state (runs_store) and a per-round spend/step ceiling (budget_guard) that aborts to a resumable checkpoint. run_manager.shutdown() must stay in the app.py lifespan finally-block or tasks leak (CLAUDE.md gotcha).

name: MCP Servers & Subprocess Infra
responsibility: The MCP protocol surface: FastMCP tool projection from the capability catalog (mcp_server.py), the internal MCP client used to call the two bundled MCP subprocesses (openbb, sec-edgar), and the Rust sidecar-spawn wrappers that own their port-wait and lifecycle per the 'always spawn via Tauri shell().sidecar(), never subprocess.Popen' rule.

name: Rust / Tauri Core
responsibility: Desktop shell: window/menu setup, OS-keychain bridge (keychain_set/get/delete), the kill-switch Tauri command surface, and app lifecycle (lib.rs wires sidecar spawn + all Tauri commands). No `cargo test` runs the built binary — only the smoke test does (CLAUDE.md gotcha), so this subsystem's tests are effectively the smoke-test script, not a Rust test file.

name: Frontend Stores (Zustand)
responsibility: The Zustand state layer shared across every panel: ~35 stores plus their colocated .test.ts files. Cross-cutting stores already owned elsewhere (portfolios, screener, backtest, plugins, marketplace, workspace, agent-runs, model-catalog/selection/llm-providers/provider-keys, proposed-changes) are excluded to avoid duplicate ownership — see their named subsystems.

name: Frontend Panels: Agent & Chat Shell
responsibility: The composer + chat surface: depth/model/persona controls, the plus-menu, mention/slash pickers, streaming markdown render, the custom-agent builder form, and the onboarding/command-palette chrome that wraps it. FLAG: message-notices.ts and streaming.ts (in this directory) are owned by error-layer, not here.

name: Frontend Panels: Chart, Watchlist & Notes
responsibility: lightweight-charts integration (drawings, ichimoku/volume-profile custom primitives, the single-sourced chart-theme palette callers must keep in lockstep with tokens.css), the watchlist list panel, and the Tiptap-based notes editor with wiki-link/slash extensions.

name: Frontend Panels: Platform Shell & Settings Chrome
responsibility: The dockview PanelHost mount + shared chrome every panel sits inside: status bar, settings panel, the generic DataTable/DataBadges/EmptyState primitives every domain panel composes, and the platform-level workspace-open dialog. This is the shallow-module risk surface — check how many panels reimplement empty/error state instead of using EmptyState.

name: Host Actions & Proposed Changes
responsibility: The gate every agent-completable write (notes, screens, layouts, paper-portfolio) passes through before landing: host-actions.ts is the always-consumed command channel, proposed-changes.ts the review/accept/reject queue rendered by ChatSidebar's ProposedChangesReview. Never bypassed for order placement per Boundaries.

name: Workspace & Layout Persistence
responsibility: SerializedWorkspace: the one blob every persisted UI field must ride (never localStorage), the viewport-fit-aware Arrange templates that downgrade a panel-heavy layout on a small screen, and the sidecar-side workspace store the frontend syncs against.

name: Scripts & Build Tooling
responsibility: The ensure-*/staleness/smoke-test orchestration that PyInstaller-builds and health-checks the three sidecar binaries, plus macOS dev-signing scripts and design-token drift auditing. No dedicated test files — smoke-test-sidecars.mjs IS the test for the sidecar build; these scripts have no unit coverage of their own, a census-worthy gap for a critic to flag.

name: Safety Model & Audit Log (§6.5, Tier-1 locked)
responsibility: The order-safety boundary end to end: the append-only audit_orders DB trigger, the kill switch (Rust command + Python service), session-scoped disclaimer acks, and the frontend confirm/audit-viewer UI. Highest-stakes subsystem in the census — CLAUDE.md forbids weakening any layer without operator sign-off; gate 8 re-proves it byte-identical at every rc. FLAG: action_ledger.py (agent-tools) and static_ip_detector.py (brokers-adapters) are also part of this defense-in-depth chain.

name: Market Data Providers (India + Global) (part 1/3)
responsibility: The largest single subsystem: every raw external data feed (NSE/BSE/yfinance/ccxt/Yahoo batch), the provider_registry dispatch point every router calls through (preference-order fallthrough, never a hardcoded if-switch), the correctness_gate that rejects a stale or impossible value before it reaches a router, and the earnings/analyst/news/SEC-filings/equity-overview panels that render the results. Almost certainly needs a second split pass once actual LOC is in (see loc field) — candidate cut: US-SEC-filings vertical vs India/global market-data vertical.

name: Market Data Providers (India + Global) (part 2/3)
responsibility: The largest single subsystem: every raw external data feed (NSE/BSE/yfinance/ccxt/Yahoo batch), the provider_registry dispatch point every router calls through (preference-order fallthrough, never a hardcoded if-switch), the correctness_gate that rejects a stale or impossible value before it reaches a router, and the earnings/analyst/news/SEC-filings/equity-overview panels that render the results. Almost certainly needs a second split pass once actual LOC is in (see loc field) — candidate cut: US-SEC-filings vertical vs India/global market-data vertical.

name: Market Data Providers (India + Global) (part 3/3)
responsibility: The largest single subsystem: every raw external data feed (NSE/BSE/yfinance/ccxt/Yahoo batch), the provider_registry dispatch point every router calls through (preference-order fallthrough, never a hardcoded if-switch), the correctness_gate that rejects a stale or impossible value before it reaches a router, and the earnings/analyst/news/SEC-filings/equity-overview panels that render the results. Almost certainly needs a second split pass once actual LOC is in (see loc field) — candidate cut: US-SEC-filings vertical vs India/global market-data vertical.

name: Macro & Quant Engines
responsibility: Two self-contained analytical engines bundled together for one critic: macro (FRED/ECB/IMF/World Bank series with a router that picks the right one) and quant (options greeks, bond pricing, Monte Carlo, yield curve), each with its own panel and store.

name: Broker Adapters (Read-Only Wrapper Layer)
responsibility: Seven broker integrations, each enforced read-only by three layers (no insert_/update_/place_ methods on the public surface, no non-GET routes, supportsControlPlane=false) audited by inspect.getmembers/router.routes tests. Kite is the deepest integration (read-only sidecar-side OAuth login + granular positions/holdings/margins reads); the plugin wrappers declare the same capability at the TypeScript contract layer.

name: Workflow / Node-Graph Engine
responsibility: @xyflow/react node-graph automation: the DAG execution engine, the per-domain node adapters (each a thin wrapper re-dispatching into its own domain — macro/quant/research/screener/sec), the sandboxed code_node, and the editor panel (palette, save dialog, run-overlay). FLAG: the *_nodes.py files each duplicate a thin slice of their domain subsystem's responsibility — check for logic that leaked here instead of staying in the domain service.
